paragraphs: We are a facilities-based provider of low-cost, high-speed Internet access, private network services, optical wavelength and optical transport services and data center colocation space and power. Our network is specifically designed and optimized to transmit packet-routed data. We deliver our services to a diverse global base of businesses, communications service providers and other bandwidth-intensive organizations in 57 countries across North America, Europe, South America, Asia, Oceania and Africa. We are a Delaware corporation headquartered in Washington, DC.

We provide our on-net Internet access and private network services to corporate, net-centric and enterprise customers. Our corporate customers are typically located in multi-tenant office buildings and consist of law firms, financial services firms, advertising and marketing firms, health care providers, educational institutions and other professional services businesses. Our net-centric customers include access networks comprised of other internet service providers ("ISPs"), telephone companies, mobile operators and cable television companies as well as bandwidth-intensive users that leverage our network to deliver content to end users. Content delivery customers include over the top media service providers, content delivery networks, web hosting companies, and commercial content and application software providers. These net-centric customers generally receive our services in carrier neutral colocation facilities or in our own data centers. We operate data centers throughout North America and Europe that allow our customers to collocate their equipment and access our network. Additionally, as part of our acquisition of the Cogent Fiber Business (as defined below) we acquired a number of "Enterprise" customers that are larger than our historical customer base. We have continued to serve these acquired Enterprise customers and have expanded our target market to include these larger Enterprise customers.

In addition to on-net services delivered via our own facilities, we provide Internet access and private network services to customers not located in buildings directly connected to our network. We provide these "off-net" services primarily to corporate customers using third-party carriers' circuits to provide the "last mile" portion of the link from the customers' premises to our network. We also provide certain non-core services that resulted from acquisitions, including the acquisition of Cogent Fiber Business, although we do not actively sell these non-core services.

In connection with our acquisition of Cogent Fiber Business, we introduced optical wavelength and optical transport services over a network that is generally independent of our legacy IP network. We offer these wavelength and optical transport services to customers who require dedicated optical transport connectivity without the capital and ongoing expenses associated with owning and operating their own network infrastructure.

On May 1, 2023 (the "Closing Date"), Cogent Infrastructure, Inc., (now Cogent Infrastructure, LLC), a Delaware corporation and our direct wholly owned subsidiary (the "Buyer" or "Cogent Infrastructure"), closed on its acquisition of the U.S. long-haul fiber network (including the non-U.S. extensions thereof) of Sprint Communications and its Subsidiaries (the "Cogent Fiber Business") in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement"), dated September 6, 2022, by and among us, Sprint Communications LLC, a Kansas limited liability company ("Sprint Communications") and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of T-Mobile US, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("T-Mobile"), and Sprint LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of T-Mobile (the "Seller"). On the Closing Date, we purchased from the Seller all of the issued and outstanding membership interests (the "Purchased Interests") of Wireline Network Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company that, following an internal restructuring and divisive merger, holds Sprint Communications' assets and liabilities relating to the Cogent Fiber Business (such transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement, collectively, the "Transaction").
The Company operates through its two direct, wholly owned subsidiaries, Cogent Infrastructure and Cogent Communications Group, LLC ("Cogent Group").

Cogent Infrastructure holds the Cogent Fiber Business assets and operations. Following the Closing Date, Cogent Infrastructure, through its subsidiaries, owned, among other things, the Sprint Network (as defined below), consisting of approximately 23,500 route miles of owned fiber optic cable in the continental United States, a portfolio of owned and leased properties totaling approximately 1.9 million square feet, Sprint operating subsidiaries in approximately 10 countries worldwide, vendor and supply agreements and 9.9 million IPv4 addresses. Through a series of intra-Company transactions, Cogent Infrastructure transferred its interest in the Sprint customer contracts, vendor and supply agreements and the majority of its IPv4 address holdings to Cogent Group, or its subsidiaries. Cogent Group has entered into long-term IRU and facilities prepaid lease agreements with Cogent Infrastructure.

On May 2, 2024, Cogent IPv4 LLC (the "IPv4 Issuer"), a special-purpose, bankruptcy remote, indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, issued $206.0 million aggregate principal amount of 7.924% secured IPv4 address revenue notes, Series 2024-1 Class A-2 (the "Existing IPv4 Notes"), with an anticipated term ending in May 2029 (such anticipated repayment date, the "ARD"), in an offering exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). On April 11, 2025 (the "New IPv4 Notes Closing Date"), IPv4 Issuer issued $174.4 million aggregate principal amount of 6.646% secured IPv4 address revenue notes, Series 2025-1 Class A-2 (collectively, the "New IPv4 Notes"), with an anticipated repayment date in April 2030, in an offering exempt from registration under the Securities Act. Our Existing IPv4 Notes and our New IPv4 Notes are collectively referred to as our $380.4 million "IPv4 Notes".

Cogent Group is the parent of Cogent Communications, LLC (formerly Cogent Communications, Inc.), which was our sole operating company prior to the Closing Date, and Cogent Group is the issuer of our $750.0 million of 7.00% senior unsecured notes due in June 2027 of which $450.0 million were issued in June 2022 ("2027 Notes") and $300.0 million were issued in June 2024 ("2027 Mirror Notes") and our $600.0 million of 6.50% senior secured notes due July 2032 ("2032 Notes") that were issued in June 2025. Cogent Group owns, among other things, our indefeasible-right-of-use ("IRU") network comprised of a portion of the Cogent Infrastructure network and third-party networks, leased Cogent data centers, Cogent operating subsidiaries in 57 countries worldwide, our customer base except for certain IPv4 leasing customers owned by the IPv4 Issuer, and over 25 million IPv4 addresses. Cogent Group also receives payments due from T-Mobile for IP transit services provided in connection with the Transaction.

We have moved and may continue to move, to the extent permitted by and in compliance with the indentures governing our 2027 Notes, 2027 Mirror Notes, 2032 Notes and our IPv4 Notes, certain assets and obligations between the companies owned by Cogent Infrastructure and Cogent Group to better align these assets and obligations with our business and operations and for general corporate purposes.

We believe we address many of the data communications needs of a diverse group of businesses, communications service providers and other bandwidth-intensive organizations by offering high-quality, high-speed Internet access, optical transport and optical wave services, and private network services at attractive prices. We believe that our organization has the following competitive advantages:

Low Cost of Operation. We believe that the wireline telecom industry is undergoing, and will continue to face, significant price deflation for its applications and services. This price deflation is a result of a variety of factors including increased competition, enhanced substitutability of certain products and services and the continued impact of Moore's Law, which has driven down the cost of technology, particularly for fiber optic Wavelength Division Multiplexing equipment and optically interfaced routers. Faced with the backdrop of continued price deflation in our industry, we have made a series of discreet choices around our network design, operating strategy and product offerings that are consistent with our objective of becoming the low-cost operator in our industry. Since our initiation of operations, this strategy has resulted in a rapid decline in our cost to transmit bits, which has increased our margins and decreased our capital intensity, excluding capital expenditures for the repurposing of acquired Sprint assets, as measured by our capital expenditures per total revenues. Important components of our low-cost operating strategy include:

● One IP Network Protocol. Upon our founding, we selected to operate our network that provides Internet - based services (our "IP Network") solely using Ethernet protocol. We made this selection in order to take advantage of the significantly greater installed base and lower cost of Ethernet network equipment versus other protocols, the substantially lower costs associated with operating and maintaining one network protocol and the continued benefits of the rapid price performance ratio improvements of Ethernet-related equipment. Our single network protocol allows us to avoid many of the costs that our competitors who operate circuit-switched, time-division multiplexing ("TDM") and hybrid fiber coaxial networks incur related to provisioning, monitoring and maintaining multiple transport protocols. Selecting one operating protocol has positively impacted our operating overhead and the simplicity of our organization. We believe the vast majority of our competitors currently operate their networks with multiple protocols, and we believe that attempts to upgrade their networks to one protocol would be operationally challenging and costly.

● Our IP Network. We have acquired a large portfolio of dark fiber leases from over 380 dark fiber vendors from around the world sourced from the excess inventory of existing networks. The nature of this portfolio and the individual leases provide us long-term access to dark fiber at attractive rates and, in many cases, the opportunity to extend these leases for multiple terms. On average, a modest number of our dark fiber leases come up for renewal each year. In addition, with our acquisition of the Cogent Fiber Business, we now own a nationwide domestic fiber network (the "Sprint Network"). Acquiring the Sprint Network allows us to capitalize on the benefits of owning network without significant upfront capital investment. The Sprint Network is mostly complementary to our existing leased dark fiber network, offers unique geographic routes and will allow us to reduce our reliance on leased dark fiber. This strategic combination of owned and leased dark fiber will help to ensure a robust and reliable network and enables us to connect via dark fiber to virtually any geographic route or facility we require on a long-term, cost-effective basis.

headings: Market Risks
Our growth and financial health are subject to a number of economic risks.
Historical reductions in our prices are expected to continue in an inflationary economy even as our costs may increase.
Events beyond our control may impact our ability to provide our services to our customers or increase the costs or reduce the profitability of providing our services.
Risks Relating to Our Acquisition of the Cogent Fiber Business
We may not realize the anticipated benefits of the acquisition of the Cogent Fiber Business, and the integration of the Cogent Fiber Business may disrupt our business and management.
Business Risks
We need to retain profitable existing customers and continue to add new customers in order to become consistently profitable and cash flow positive.
A substantial and long-term shift to remote work may impact our ability to add new customers and to retain existing customers.
Lower vacancy rates as a result of diminished lease terminations and increased leasing and subleasing activity will be a key factor in driving renewed growth in our corporate business.
Our business and operations are growing rapidly, and we may not be able to efficiently manage our growth.
We may be unable to retain existing enterprise customers, maintain the level of services provided to enterprise customers or attract new enterprise customers.
Demand from certain employees to work remotely may reduce the attractiveness of our business as an employer versus some competitors who are allowing employees to work remotely.
We may not successfully make or integrate acquisitions or enter into strategic alliances.
Our data center expansions could involve significant risks to our business.
Our ability to maintain or grow revenue from leasing IPv4 addresses is subject to factors beyond our control.
We may be unable to monetize our data center or IPv4 assets.
Our commitments and disclosures regarding environmental, social, and governance ("ESG") matters expose us to potential reputational and legal risks.
Competitive Risks
Our connections to the Internet require us to establish and maintain relationships with other providers, which we may not be able to maintain.
The sector in which we operate is highly competitive, and we may not be able to compete effectively.
Our Optical Wave Network footprint is connected primarily to CNDCs, which may not allow us to serve the entire addressable market.

Our business could suffer because telephone companies and cable companies may provide better delivery of certain Internet content, including content originating on their own networks, than content on the public Internet.
Operational Risks
Our networks may be the target of potential cyber-attacks and other security breaches that could have significant negative consequences.
Our insurance coverage may be insufficient to fully protect against potential risks.
Our IPv4 address space is now covered by Resource Public Key Infrastructure ("RPKI") which may not fully protect against potential risks.
Network Augmentation and Maintenance Risks
Our networks are comprised of a number of separate components, and we may be unable to obtain or maintain the agreements necessary to augment or maintain our networks.
Our off-net business could suffer delays and problems due to the actions of "last mile" providers on whom we are partially dependent.
Our business could suffer from an interruption of service from our fiber providers.
With the Cogent Fiber Business acquisition, our reliance on agreements with landowners has increased.
Effects of climate change may impose risk of damage to our infrastructure and our ability to provide services.
We are responsible for maintenance and repair of our owned fiber network.
Substantially all of our network infrastructure equipment is manufactured or provided by a limited number of network infrastructure vendors.
International Operations Risks
Our international operations expose us to numerous risks.
Our international operations involve a number of risks, including:
Litigation Risks
As an Internet service provider, we may incur liabilities for the content disseminated through our network or for network failures, delays or errors in transmissions.

paragraphs: A downturn in the world economy, especially the economies of North America and Europe, would negatively impact our growth. Our net-centric business would be particularly impacted by a decline in the development of new Internet-based applications and

businesses that make use of the Internet. Our corporate business would be particularly impacted by an increase in vacancy rates in the MTOBs that we serve. Growth in our IP-transit segment is predicated on growth in the use of the Internet to offset the declining prices of Internet service. An economic downturn could impact the Internet business more significantly than other businesses that are less dependent on new Internet-based applications and growth in the use of those applications and less susceptible to increases in office vacancy rates resulting from the retrenchment by consumers and businesses that typically occurs in an economic downturn.

Many of the regions in which we operate continue to experience an increase in or elevated inflation rates. Due to the nature of our product offerings and the industry in which we operate, which is deflationary, we may be unable to raise our prices. We expect that our historical pricing patterns will continue for the foreseeable future. Additionally, we may be unable to achieve the sales volume necessary to compensate for price reductions, which may adversely impact our revenue growth.

These historical pricing patterns are occurring against the backdrop of a general increase in prices due to inflation. In particular, the cost of electricity has increased in all countries where we purchase power. While, in certain cases, we have negotiated contracts that cap price increases due to inflation or that have fixed the price of electricity, we have experienced and may continue to experience increases in the costs of electricity and other services that we cannot pass on to our customers or may only be able to pass on partially to our customers. If these price increases continue, this may impact our profitability.

Catastrophic events, such as major natural disasters, extreme weather events (including those exacerbated by climate change), fire, flooding, public health crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic or similar events as well as the continued threat of terrorist activity and other acts of war or hostility have had, and may continue to have, an adverse effect on our headquarters, other offices, our networks, infrastructure or equipment or our customers and prospective customers, which could adversely affect our business. These events may also have an adverse impact on business, financial and general economic conditions around the world. We have certain locations through which a large amount of our Internet traffic passes. Examples are facilities in which we exchange traffic with other carriers, the facilities through which our transoceanic traffic passes, and certain of our network hub sites. We also rely on third-party data centers and service providers in these regions whose own disaster recovery capabilities are beyond our control. We are particularly vulnerable to acts of terrorism because our largest customer concentration is located in New York, our headquarters is located in Washington, D.C., and we have significant operations in Paris, Madrid and London, cities that have historically been targets for terrorist attacks and may be vulnerable to extreme weather and public health crises.

If these or any other of our key facilities or those of our critical third-party providers were destroyed or seriously damaged, a significant amount of our network traffic could be disrupted. Because of the large volume of traffic passing through these facilities our ability (and the ability of carriers with whom we exchange traffic) to quickly restore service would be challenged. There could be parts of our networks or the networks of other carriers that could not be quickly restored or that would experience substantially reduced service for a significant time. Such disruptions may also increase our vulnerability to cybersecurity attacks, further complicating recovery efforts. If such a disruption occurs, our reputation could be negatively impacted, which may cause us to lose customers and adversely affect our ability to attract new customers, resulting in an adverse effect on our business and operating results. While we maintain business continuity plans and insurance coverage, these measures may not be sufficient to fully mitigate the financial or operational impact of such events.

The discussion in this report contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties, such as statements of our plans, objectives, expectations and intentions. The cautionary statements made in this report should be read as applying to all related forward-looking statements wherever they appear in this report. Factors that could cause or contribute to these differences include those discussed in "Item 1A. Risk Factors," as well as those discussed elsewhere. You should read "Item 1A. Risk Factors" and "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements." Our actual results could differ materially from those discussed here. Factors that could cause or contribute to these differences include, but are not limited to:

Our acquisition of Sprint Communications, now called Cogent Fiber, LLC, including difficulties integrating our business with the Cogent Fiber Business, which may result in the combined company not operating as effectively and efficiently as expected; government policies worldwide; vaccination and in-office requirements, delays in the delivery of network equipment or optical fiber, loss of key right-of-way agreements, future economic instability in the global economy, including the risk of economic recession and bank failures and liquidity concerns at certain other banks, which could affect spending on Internet services; the impact of changing foreign exchange rates (in particular the Euro to US dollar and Canadian dollar to US dollar exchange rates) on the translation of our non-US dollar denominated revenues, expenses, assets and liabilities into US dollars; legal and operational difficulties in new markets; our ability to maintain our regulatory licenses that are required in the markets in which we operate; the imposition of a requirement that we contribute to the US Universal Service Fund on the basis of our Internet revenue; changes in government policy and/or regulation, including rules regarding data protection, cyber security and net neutrality; increasing competition leading to lower prices for our services; our ability to attract new customers and to increase and maintain the volume of traffic on our network; the ability to maintain our Internet peering and right-of-way arrangements on favorable terms; our ability to renew our long-term leases of optical fiber and right-of-way agreements that comprise our network; our reliance on a limited number of equipment vendors, and the potential for hardware or software problems associated with such equipment; our inability to obtain the equipment necessary for our expansion plans and customer requirements; tariffs imposed on equipment we purchase for our network or other similar government-imposed fees and charges; the dependence of our network on the quality and dependability of third-party fiber and right-of-way providers; our ability to retain certain customers that comprise a significant portion of our revenue base; the management of network failures and/or disruptions; our ability to make payments on our indebtedness as they become due and outcomes in litigation, risks associated with variable interest rates under our Swap Agreement as well as other risks discussed from time to time in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including, without limitation, this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and our Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q.

On May 1, 2023 (the "Closing Date"), Cogent Infrastructure, Inc. (now Cogent Infrastructure, LLC), a Delaware corporation and our direct wholly owned subsidiary (the "Buyer", "Cogent Infrastructure", "we" or "us"), closed on its acquisition of the U.S. long-haul fiber network (including the non-U.S. extensions thereof) of Sprint Communications and its subsidiaries (the "Cogent Fiber Business") in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement"), dated September 6, 2022, by and among us, Sprint Communications LLC, a Kansas limited liability company ("Sprint Communications") and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of T-Mobile US, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("T-Mobile"), and Sprint LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of T-Mobile (the "Seller"). On the Closing Date, we purchased from the Seller all of the issued and outstanding membership interests (the "Purchased Interests") of Wireline Network Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company that, following an internal restructuring and divisive merger, held Sprint Communications' assets and liabilities relating to the Cogent Fiber Business (such transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement, collectively, the "Transaction").

On the Closing Date, we consummated the Transaction pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Agreement, providing a purchase price of $1 payable to the Seller for the Purchased Interests, subject to customary adjustments, including working capital (the "Working Capital Adjustment"), as set forth in the Purchase Agreement. As consideration for the Purchased Interests, the Working Capital Adjustment (primarily related to acquired cash and cash equivalents of an estimated $43.4 million at the Closing Date in order

to fund the international operations of the Cogent Fiber Business) resulted in us making a payment to the Seller of $61.1 million on the Closing Date. In April 2024, an additional Working Capital Adjustment of $5.0 million was paid to the Seller.

The Purchase Agreement provides for a payment of $28.1 million ($19.8 million net of discount) from the Seller to us related to acquired short - term operating lease obligations (the "Short - term Lease Payment"). The Short - term Lease Payment will be paid from the Seller to us in four equal payments in months 55 to 58 after the Closing Date. The final determination of the Short - term Lease Payment was completed in April 2024. The Short - term Lease Payment was recorded at its present value resulting in a discount of $8.4 million. The interest rate used in determining the present value was derived considering rates on similar issued debt instruments with comparable durations, among other market factors. The determination of the discount rate requires some judgment. During the third quarter of 2023, the Short - term Lease Payment was reduced by $4.8 million and in the first quarter of 2024 the Short - term Lease Payment, net of discount, was reduced by an additional $17.0 million.

On the Closing Date, we entered into an agreement for IP transit services ("IP Transit Services Agreement"), pursuant to which TMUSA will pay us an aggregate of $700.0 million, consisting of (i) $350.0 million in equal monthly installments of $29.2 million per month during the first year after the Closing Date and (ii) $350.0 million in equal monthly installments of $8.3 million per month over the subsequent 42 months. Under the IP Transit Services Agreement., TMUSA paid us $100.0 million, $204.2 million and $204.2 million during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

We accounted for the Transaction as a business combination under ASC Topic 805 Business Combinations ("ASC 805"). We evaluated what elements are part of the business combination and the consideration exchanged to complete the acquisition. Under ASC 805, we concluded that the $700.0 million of payments to be made represent consideration received from T-Mobile to complete the acquisition of a distressed business. We also evaluated whether the IP Transit Services Agreement was in the scope of ASU No. 2014-09 Revenue from Contracts with Customers ("ASC 606"). We concluded that T-Mobile did not represent a "customer" as defined by ASC 606, the stated contract price did not represent consideration for services to be delivered, and the transaction did not satisfy the definition of revenue, which excluded this arrangement from the scope of ASC 606. As a result, and considering statements made by T-Mobile, the IP Transit Services Agreement was recorded in connection with the Transaction at its discounted present value resulting in a discount of $79.6 million. The interest rate used in determining the present value was derived considering rates on similar issued debt instruments with comparable durations, among other market factors. The determination of the discount rate requires some judgment.

On the Closing Date, we entered into a transition services agreement (the "TSA") with the Seller, pursuant to which the Seller provides to us, and we provide to the Seller on an interim basis following the Closing Date, certain specified services (the "Transition Services") to ensure an orderly transition following the separation of the Cogent Fiber Business from Sprint Communications. The services provided by the Seller to us include, among others, information technology support, back office and finance, real estate and facilities, vendor and supply chain management, including the payment and processing of vendor invoices for the Company and human resources. The services provided by us to the Seller include, among others, information technology and network support, finance and back office and other wireless business support.

The Transition Services are generally intended to be provided for a period of up to two years following the Closing Date, although such period may be extended for an additional one-year term by either party upon 30 days' prior written notice. The fees for the Transition Services are calculated using either a per service monthly fee or an hourly rate for the employees allocated to provide such services. Any third-party costs incurred in providing the Transition Services are passed on to the party receiving such services at cost for the two-year period. Amounts paid for the Cogent Fiber Business by T-Mobile are reimbursed at cost.

Either party to the TSA may terminate the agreement with respect to any individual service in full for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice for certain services and reduced for other services after a 90-day period. The TSA may be terminated in its entirety if the other party has failed to perform any of its material obligations and such failure is not cured within 30 days. The TSA provides for customary indemnification and limits on liability. Amounts billed under the TSA are due 30 days from receipt of the related invoice. Amounts billed to us under the TSA are primarily for reimbursement at cost of payments to vendors of the Cogent Fiber Business until these vendors are fully transitioned to us.

During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we were billed $0.4 million, $27.2 million and $284.1 million, respectively, as due to the Seller under the TSA. During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we paid to the Seller $1.0 million, $93.8 million and $217.2 million, respectively, under the TSA. Amounts billed under the TSA are due 30 days from receipt of the related invoice.

During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we billed the Seller $0.2 million, $1.1 million and $6.2 million, respectively, as due from the Seller under the TSA. During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Seller paid us $0.2 million, $1.3 million and $6.0 million, respectively, under the TSA.

The Purchase Agreement also provides for reimbursement from the Seller to us for qualifying severance expenses incurred. Total qualifying severance expenses were $28.6 million of which $12.3 million and $16.2 million were recorded during the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, and fully reimbursed by the Seller. These severance payments ended in the second quarter of 2024.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間以設施為基礎的低成本、高速度網際網路存取服務、私人網路服務、光波長及光傳輸服務、以及資料中心共置空間與電力供應服務的提供者。我們的網路特別設計並優化以傳送封包路由資料。我們將服務提供給遍及北美、歐洲、南美、亞洲、大洋洲及非洲57個國家的多樣性全球企業、通訊服務供應商及其他高頻寬需求機構。本公司為德拉瓦州公司，總部設於華盛頓特區。

我們為企業客戶、網路中心客戶及企業客戶提供網內網際網路存取及私人網路服務。企業客戶通常位於多租戶辦公大樓內，包括律師事務所、金融服務機構、廣告與行銷機構、醫療機構、教育機構及其他專業服務機構。網路中心客戶包括由其他網際網路服務供應商（"ISPs"）、電信業者、行動運營商及有線電視公司組成的存取網路，以及利用我們網路將內容傳遞給終端用戶的高頻寬需求用戶。內容傳輸客戶包括過頂媒體服務供應商、內容傳輸網路、網站主機公司及商業內容與應用軟體供應商。這些網路中心客戶通常在電信中立共置設施或我們自己的資料中心接收我們的服務。我們在北美及歐洲運營資料中心，使客戶能夠共置其設備並存取我們的網路。此外，根據我們收購Cogent Fiber Business（如下所定）的交易，我們收購了若干較我們歷史客戶羣更大的"企業"客戶。我們持續為這些收購的企業客戶提供服務，並已擴展目標市場以包含這些較大的企業客戶。
除了透過我們自己的設施提供的網內服務，我們也為不在直接連接到我們網路的建築物內的客戶提供網際網路存取及私人網路服務。我們主要透過第三方電信業者的電路為這些"網外"客戶提供服務，以完成從客戶場地到我們網路的"最後一哩"連接。我們也提供某些非核心服務，這些服務來自收購，包括收購Cogent Fiber Business，但我們並未積極銷售這些非核心服務。
根據我們收購Cogent Fiber Business的交易，我們在一個通常與我們遺留IP網路無關的網路中引入光波長及光傳輸服務。我們向需要專用光傳輸連線的客戶提供這些波長及光傳輸服務，而這些客戶不需要擁有並運營自己的網路基礎設施所帶來的資本與持續支出。

於2023年5月1日（"成交日"），Cogent Infrastructure, Inc.（現為Cogent Infrastructure, LLC），一間德拉瓦州公司且為我們的直接 wholly owned 子公司（"買方"或"Cogent Infrastructure"），根據2022年9月6日簽訂的會員權益購買協議（"購買協議"）的條款與條件，完成了對Sprint Communications及其子公司美國長途光纖網路（包括非美國延伸部分）的收購。於成交日，我們從賣方購入Wireline Network Holdings LLC全部已發行及流通的會員權益（"購入權益"），該公司為德拉瓦州有限責任公司，於內部重整及分割合併後，持有Sprint Communications與Cogent Fiber Business相關的資產與負債。這些交易（購買協議所規定的交易） collectively 稱為"交易"。
本公司透過其兩間直接、 wholly owned 子公司Cogent Infrastructure及Cogent Communications Group, LLC（"Cogent Group"）運營。

Cogent Infrastructure持有Cogent Fiber Business的資產與運營。於成交日後，Cogent Infrastructure透過其子公司擁有，包括其他項目，Sprint Network（如下所定），包含約23,500英里擁有光纖電纜的美國大陸地區，約190萬平方英尺的擁有及租賃物業，約10個國家的Sprint運營子公司，供應商與供應協議，以及約990萬個IPv4位址。透過一系列公司內交易，Cogent Infrastructure已將其在Sprint客戶合約、供應商與供應協議及大部分IPv4位址持有權轉讓至Cogent Group或其子公司。Cogent Group已與Cogent Infrastructure簽訂長期IRU及設施預付租賃協議。

於2024年5月2日，Cogent IPv4 LLC（"IPv4發行者"），本公司一間特殊目的、破產遠離、間接 wholly owned 子公司，發行了總金額206.0百萬美元的7.924% secured IPv4位址收入票據，Series 2024-1 Class A-2（"現有IPv4票據"），預期還款日期為2029年5月（此預期還款日期稱為"ARD"），此發行在1933年證券法（"證券法"）修正案下免於註冊。於2025年4月11日（"新IPv4票據成交日"），IPv4發行者發行了總金額174.4百萬美元的6.646% secured IPv4位址收入票據，Series 2025-1 Class A-2（ collectively 稱為"新IPv4票據"），預期還款日期為2030年4月，此發行在證券法修正案下免於註冊。我們的現有IPv4票據與新IPv4票據 collectively 稱為我們380.4百萬美元的"IPv4票據"。

Cogent Group 是 Cogent Communications, LLC (原為 Cogent Communications, Inc.) 的母公司，該公司為我們在 Closing Date 之前唯一的營運公司，且 Cogent Group 是我們 $750.0 百萬的 7.00% 高級無擔保票據於 2027 年 6 月到期 (稱為 "2027 Notes") 的發行者，其中 $450.0 百萬於 2022 年 6 月發行 ("2027 Notes")，$300.0 百萬於 2024 年 6 月發行 ("2027 Mirror Notes")，以及我們 $600.0 百萬的 6.50% 高級有擔保票據於 2032 年 7 月到期 ("2032 Notes")，該票據於 2025 年 6 月發行。Cogent Group 擁有，包括但不限於，我們的不可撤銷使用權 ("IRU") 網路，包含 Cogent 基礎設施網路及第三方網路的一部分，租賃的 Cogent 資料中心，Cogent 在全球 57 個國家的營運子公司，我們的客戶羣除了由 IPv4 發行者所擁有特定的 IPv4 租賃客戶外，以及超過 25 百萬的 IPv4 位址。Cogent Group 也會收到來自 T-Mobile 的 IP 通訊服務付款。
我們已將並可能持續將，在符合我們 2027 Notes、2027 Mirror Notes、2032 Notes 及我們 IPv4 Notes 的契約條款下，Cogent 基礎設施與 Cogent Group 所擁有公司的某些資產與義務，以更好地將這些資產與義務與我們的業務與營運對齊，並用於一般企業用途。
我們相信我們能透過提供高品質、高速的網路存取、光學運輸與光波服務，以及私有網路服務，以有競爭力的價格，來滿足多樣化的企業、通訊服務供應商及其他大量使用頻寬組織的資料通訊需求。我們相信我們的組織擁有以下競爭優勢：

低運作成本。我們認為線路電信產業正在經歷，並將持續面對其應用與服務的重大價格下跌。這種價格下跌是因為多種因素，包括增加的競爭、某些產品與服務的替代性提高，以及摩爾定律的持續影響，這已驅動技術成本下降，特別是對於光纖光波分複用設備與光學介面路由器。面對我們產業持續的價格下跌背景，我們已做出一系列與我們成為產業中低成本運營商目標一致的網路設計、運營策略與產品提供的選擇。自我們開始營運以來，這項策略已導致我們每傳輸一位元的成本迅速下降，這已提高我們的毛利率，並降低我們的資本強度（不包括為重新利用取得的 Sprint 資產所進行的資本支出），以我們的資本支出與總營收之比來衡量。我們低運作成本運營策略的重要組成部分包括：

● 一個 IP 網路協議。我們成立時，我們選擇僅使用乙太網協議來運行我們提供基於互聯網服務的網路（我們的 "IP 網路"）。我們做出此選擇是為了利用乙太網網路設備的安裝基礎更大且成本更低，以及運行和維護一個網路協議的相對成本更低，以及乙太網相關設備的價格性能比持續改善的優勢。我們單一的網路協議使我們能避免許多競爭對手運行電路交換、時分複用 ("TDM") 和混合光纖同軸網路所產生的與 provisioning、監測和維護多種運輸協議相關的成本。選擇單一運營協議已正面影響我們的運營開支，並簡化我們的組織結構。我們相信目前絕大多數競爭對手都運行多種協議的網路，我們認為他們嘗試將網路升級為單一協議會在操作上具有挑戰性且成本高昂。

● 我們的 IP 網路。我們已從全球超過 380 家暗纖供應商取得大量暗纖租賃，這些供應商來自現有網路的閒置庫存。此組合的性質與個別租賃使我們能長期以有吸引力的價格取得暗纖，並在許多情況下有機會將這些租賃延長多個租期。平均而言，我們的暗纖租賃每年只有少數需要續約。此外，透過取得 Cogent 光纖業務，我們現在擁有全國性的國內光纖網路（"Sprint 網路"）。取得 Sprint 網路使我們能利用擁有網路的優勢，而無需大量的前期資本投資。Sprint 網路大多與我們現有的租賃暗纖網路相輔相成，提供獨特的地理路由，並使我們能減少對租賃暗纖的依賴。這種擁有與租賃暗纖的戰略組合將有助於確保一個強大且可靠的網路，並使我們能以長期且成本效益的方式透過暗纖連接到幾乎任何地理路由或設施。

paragraphs: 您應配合本報告中之討論與分析，一併閱讀我們之合併財務報表及相關附註，包含於本報告中。本報告中之討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，例如我們之計畫、目標、預期與意圖之陳述。本報告中所作之警示陳述應適用於所有相關之前瞻性陳述，無論其出現在本報告之何處。造成或導致這些差異之因素，包含於「第 1A 項 風險因素」中所討論者，以及於其他處所討論者。您應閱讀「第 1A 項 風險因素」及「關於前瞻性陳述之特別說明」。我們之實際結果可能與 herein 所討論者有重大差異。造成或導致這些差異之因素，包含但不限於：

我們取得 Sprint Communications，現稱 Cogent Fiber, LLC，包含將我們之業務與 Cogent Fiber 事業整合之困難，可能導致合併後之公司無法如預期般有效且高效運作；全球政府政策；疫苗接種與辦公室要求，網路設備或光纖之交付延誤，喪失關鍵之道路使用權協議，全球經濟未來之不穩定，包含經濟衰退與銀行失敗及某些其他銀行之流動性問題之風險，可能影響網際網路服務之支出；變動之外匯匯率（特別是歐元對美元與加拿大幣對美元之匯率）對我們非美元計價之收入、費用、資產與負債轉換為美元之影響；在新市場之法律與運營困難；我們維持我們在營運市場所需之監管許可之能力；我們被要求根據我們之網際網路收入貢獻美國通用服務基金之可能性；政府政策與/或規範之變動，包含資料保護、網路安全與網路中立性之規則；增加之競爭導致我們服務之價格下降；我們吸引新客戶之能力與增加並維持我們網路之流量；維持我們網際網路對等連接與道路使用權安排之能力；我們續約我們長期租賃之光纖與道路使用權協議之能力；我們對有限數量之設備供應商之依賴，以及與此等設備相關之硬體或軟體問題之潛在可能；我們無法取得為我們擴張計畫與客戶需求所必需之設備；對我們為網路所購買之設備所課徵之關稅或其他類似政府所課徵之費用與稅金；我們網路對第三方光纖與道路使用權供應商之品質與可靠性之依賴；我們保留某些組成我們收入基礎之重要客戶之能力；網路故障與/或中斷之管理；我們支付我們債務之能力，以及訴訟結果、我們 Swap 協議下變動利率之相關風險，以及其他在我們向證券交易委員會所提交之文件中時而討論之風險，包含但不限於本年度截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之年度報告表 10-K，以及我們之季度報告表 10-Q。

於 2023 年 5 月 1 日（「成交日」），Cogent Infrastructure, Inc.（現為 Cogent Infrastructure, LLC），一家特拉華州公司，為我們之直接全資子公司（「買方」、「Cogent Infrastructure」、「我們」或「我們」），根據 2022 年 9 月 6 日由我們、Sprint Communications LLC，一家堪薩斯州有限責任公司（「Sprint Communications」）與 T-Mobile US, Inc.，一家特拉華州公司之間間接全資子公司（「T-Mobile」）以及 Sprint LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司且為 T-Mobile 之間接全資子公司（「賣方」）所簽訂之會員權益購買協議（「購買協議」）之條款與條件，完成對 Sprint Communications 及其子公司之美國長途光纖網路（包含非美國之延伸部分）之收購。於成交日，我們自賣方購入 Wireline Network Holdings LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司之全部發行與在冊會員權益（「購入權益」），該公司於內部重整與分割合併後，持有 Sprint Communications 有關 Cogent Fiber 事業之資產與負債（購買協議中所預期之交易， collectively 稱為「交易」）。
於成交日，我們根據購買協議之條款完成交易，提供給賣方購入權益之對價為 1 美元，並根據常規調整，包含營運資金（「營運資金調整」），如購買協議中所載。作為購入權益之對價，營運資金調整（主要與於成交日購入之現金及現金等價物預估為 43.4 百萬美元有關）

買賣協議規定，賣方應支付我們28.1 百萬美元（折讓後為19.8 百萬美元）與取得的短期營運租賃義務相關（稱為"短期租賃付款"）。短期租賃付款將於閉盤日後第55至58個月以四筆相等金額支付給我們。短期租賃付款的最終確定於2024年4月完成。短期租賃付款以現值入賬，產生8.4 百萬美元的折讓。用以計算現值的利率係根據類似發行債務工具的利率及其他市場因素決定。折讓率的確定需要一定的判斷。2023年第三季，短期租賃付款減少4.8 百萬美元；2024年第一季，扣除折讓後的短期租賃付款再減少17.0 百萬美元。

於閉盤日，我們與TMUSA簽訂IP通訊服務協議（"IP通訊服務協議"），根據該協議，TMUSA將支付我們總計700.0 百萬美元，包含（i）於閉盤日後第一年內，每月支付29.2 百萬美元，共支付350.0 百萬美元；以及（ii）於隨後42個月內，每月支付8.3 百萬美元，共支付350.0 百萬美元。根據IP通訊服務協議，TMUSA於2025年12月31日財年、2024年及2023年分別支付我們100.0 百萬美元、204.2 百萬美元及204.2 百萬美元。

我們根據ASC主題805商業結合（"ASC 805"）將此交易視為企業併購。我們評估了企業併購所包含的要素及用以完成收購的對價。根據ASC 805，我們結論認為，將支付的700.0 百萬美元代表T-Mobile為完成收購一個處境困難企業而提供的對價。我們也評估了IP通訊服務協議是否屬於ASU No. 2014-09與客戶的合同收入（"ASC 606"）的範疇。我們結論認為，T-Mobile並不符合ASC 606所定義的"客戶"，合同價格並不代表為提供服務而支付的對價，且此交易並未符合收入的定義，因此此安排排除於ASC 606的範疇。因此，並考量T-Mobile的陳述，IP通訊服務協議於交易中以折讓後的現值入賬，產生79.6 百萬美元的折讓。用以計算現值的利率係根據類似發行債務工具的利率及其他市場因素決定。折讓率的確定需要一定的判斷。

於交易完成日，本公司與賣方簽訂了轉移服務協議（the "TSA"），根據該協議，賣方提供本公司特定指定服務（the "Transition Services"），本公司亦在交易完成日後暫時提供賣方相關服務，以確保在從 Sprint Communications 分離 Cogent Fiber 事業後，能順利進行過渡。賣方提供本公司之服務包括，資訊科技支援、後臺及財務、不動產與設施、供應商與供應鏈管理，包括本公司供應商發票之付款與處理，以及人力資源。本公司提供賣方之服務包括，資訊科技與網路支援、財務與後臺及其他無線業務支援。

Transition Services 通常預期在交易完成日後提供最多兩年，不過任一方可於事前30日書面通知後，將此期間延長一年。Transition Services 之費用係根據每項服務每月費用或分配至提供該服務之員工之時薪計算。提供 Transition Services 所產生之第三方成本，於兩年期間內會轉嫁至接收該服務之當事人，按成本計算。T-Mobile 為 Cogent Fiber 事業所支付之金額，會按成本予以補償。
任一方可於事前30日書面通知後，就特定服務終止 TSA 之全部內容，對於其他服務則在90日後可終止。若任一方未履行其重大義務，且在30日內未補救，則 TSA 可終止。TSA 提供常見之賠償條款及責任限制。TSA 下所開立之帳單，應於收到相關發票後30日內結清。TSA 下本公司所支付之金額，主要是為補償 Cogent Fiber 事業供應商之付款，直至這些供應商完全過渡至本公司為止。

於截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之會計年度，本公司因TSA應支付給賣方之金額分別為27.2百萬美元、284.1百萬美元及0.4百萬美元。於截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之會計年度，本公司根據TSA支付給賣方之金額分別為93.8百萬美元、217.2百萬美元及1.0百萬美元。TSA 下所開立之帳單，應於收到相關發票後30日內結清。
於截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之會計年度，本公司因TSA應收取賣方之金額分別為1.1百萬美元、6.2百萬美元及0.2百萬美元。於截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之會計年度，賣方根據TSA支付給本公司之金額分別為1.3百萬美元、6.0百萬美元及0.2百萬美元。
購買協議亦規定賣方應向本公司補償符合條件之遣散費用。總計符合條件之遣散費用為28.6百萬美元，其中12.3百萬美元及16.2百萬美元分別於截至2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之會計年度記入，並由賣方完全補償。這些遣散費用於2024年第二季結束。

headings: 市場風險
本公司成長與財務狀況受多項經濟風險影響。
歷史價格減讓情形在通貨膨脹經濟環境下預期將持續，即使本公司成本可能增加。
我們無法控制的事件可能影響本公司提供服務予客戶的能力，或提高提供服務的成本或降低其獲利性。
與本公司收購Cogent Fiber業務相關的風險
本公司可能無法實現收購Cogent Fiber業務預期的效益，且Cogent Fiber業務的整合可能幹擾本公司業務與管理。
業務風險
本公司需維持獲利性現有客戶，並持續增加新客戶，以實現穩定獲利與現金流為正。
重大且長期的遠端工作趨勢可能影響我們增加新客戶及維持現有客戶的能力。
因租約終止減少及租賃與次租賃活動增加所導致的空置率下降，將是推動我們企業業務重啟成長的關鍵因素。
我們的業務與運作正在快速成長，我們可能無法有效管理此成長。
我們可能無法維持現有企業客戶，維持對企業客戶所提供的服務水準或吸引新企業客戶。
部分員工要求遠端工作的需求，可能降低我們作為僱主的吸引力，相較於允許員工遠端工作的競爭對手。
我們可能無法成功進行或整合收購，或進入策略聯盟。
我們的資料中心擴張可能涉及對我們業務的重大風險。
我們維持或成長來自租賃 IPv4 位址的收入能力，取決於我們無法控制的外部因素。
我們可能無法將我們的資料中心或 IPv4 資產進行商業化。
我們對於環境、社會及治理（"ESG"）事項的承諾與揭露，使我們面臨潛在的聲譽與法律風險。
競爭風險
我們與互聯網的連接需要我們與其他服務提供者建立並維持關係，而我們可能無法維持這些關係。
我們所從事的產業具有高度競爭性，我們可能無法有效地進行競爭。
我們的光波網路覆蓋範圍主要連接到 CNDCs，這可能無法讓我們服務整個可達市場。
我們的業務可能受影響，因為電信公司和有線電視公司可能提供比公共互聯網上內容更優質的某些互聯網內容，包括來自其自有網路的內容。
運營風險
我公司的網路可能成為潛在網路攻擊及其他安全漏洞的目標，這可能會導致重大負面後果。
我公司的保險覆蓋範圍可能不足以完全抵禦潛在風險。
我公司的 IPv4 位址空間現已透過 Resource Public Key Infrastructure ("RPKI") 進行覆蓋，這可能無法完全抵禦潛在風險。
網路增強與維護風險
我公司的網路由許多獨立零組件組成，我們可能無法取得或維持必要的協議以增強或維護我公司的網路。
我公司的離網業務可能因 "最後一哩" 提供商的行為而遭遇延誤與問題，而我公司對這些提供商有部分依賴。
我公司的業務可能因光纖供應商的服務中斷而受到影響。
透過 Cogent Fiber Business 收購，我公司對與土地所有者協議的依賴程度已提高。
氣候變遷的影響可能導致我們的基礎建設及提供服務的能力遭受損壞的風險。
我們負責維護及修復我們所有的光纖網路。
我們的網路基礎建設設備幾乎全部由極少數的網路基礎建設供應商製造或提供。
國際營運風險
我們的國際營運使我們面臨許多風險。
我們的國際營運涉及多種風險，包括：
訴訟風險
作為網際網路服務提供商，我們可能因透過我們網路散佈的內容或網路故障、延遲或傳輸錯誤而產生責任。
法規風險
遵守現行及擬議的隱私規範成本高昂，若本公司或我們的供應商未能遵守，可能會導致重大賠償責任、負面宣傳，以及/或信任度的流失
paragraphs: 全球經濟衰退，特別是北美與歐洲經濟，將對我們的成長造成負面影響。我們的網路中心業務將特別受到新網際網路應用程式開發減少的影響，
以及使用網際網路的企業。我們的企業業務將特別受到我們服務的MTOBs租賃空置率上升的影響。我們IP轉接業務的成長取決於網際網路使用量的成長，以抵消網際網路服務價格下降的影響。經濟衰退可能對網際網路業務造成比其他較不依賴新網際網路應用程式及這些應用程式成長，且較不受消費者與企業在經濟衰退時縮減支出所影響的業務更顯著的影響。
我們營運的許多地區持續經歷通貨膨脹率的增加或高於正常水平。由於我們產品組合的性質以及所處產業為通貨緊縮型，我們可能無法提高價格。我們預期歷史價格模式將在可預見的未來持續。此外，我們可能無法達到足夠的銷售量以彌補價格下降的影響，這可能會對我們的營收成長造成負面影響。
這些歷史價格模式是在通貨膨脹導致價格普遍上升的背景下發生的。特別是，在我們購電的國家，電力成本已增加。雖然在某些情況下，我們已談判了因應通貨膨脹而限制價格上漲的合約，或固定電力價格，但我們已經驗到並可能持續經驗到電力及其他服務成本的增加，而這些成本無法轉嫁給客戶或只能部分轉嫁給客戶。如果這些價格上漲持續，這可能會影響我們的獲利能力。

重大事件，例如重大自然災害、極端天氣事件（包括因氣候變遷而惡化的情況）、火災、水災、公共衛生危機如冠狀病毒疫情或類似事件，以及持續的恐怖攻擊威脅和其他戰爭或敵對行動，已對我們的總部、其他辦公室、我們的網路、基礎建設或設備，或客戶與潛在客戶造成負面影響，並可能持續造成負面影響。這些事件也可能對全球的業務、財務及總體經濟狀況造成負面影響。我們有一些設施，大量我們的網際網路流量經過這些設施。例如，我們與其他電信業者交換流量的設施、我們的跨洋流量經過的設施，以及某些網路核心站點。我們也依賴這些地區的第三方資料中心與服務供應商，而這些供應商的災難復原能力超出我們的控制範圍。我們特別容易受到恐怖攻擊的影響，因為我們最大的客戶集中地在紐約，總部在華盛頓特區，且我們在巴黎、馬德里與倫敦有大量營運，這些城市歷來都是恐怖攻擊的目標，且可能受到極端天氣與公共衛生危機的影響。

如果這些或任何其他我們關鍵設施，或我們關鍵第三方供應商的設施遭到破壞或嚴重損壞，我們大量網路流量可能受到幹擾。由於大量流量經過這些設施，我們（以及與我們交換流量的電信業者）迅速恢復服務的能力將受到挑戰。我們的網路或其它電信業者的網路可能有部分無法迅速恢復，或在一段相當長的時間內服務大幅下降。這種幹擾也可能增加我們對網路安全攻擊的脆弱性，進一步複雜化復原工作。如果發生這種幹擾，我們的聲譽可能受到負面影響，這可能導致我們失去客戶，並對我們吸引新客戶的能力造成負面影響，進而對我們的業務與營運成果造成負面影響。雖然我們有業務連續性計畫與保險覆蓋，但這些措施可能不足以完全彌補這些事件的財務或營運影響。
